Fix the invalid border-colour CSS property

Fixes #591.

`border-colour` is not a valid CSS property, so the `figure` rule never applied the intended white border colour. This replaces it with `border-color`.

Generated by OpenCode

Reset the path source when loading a graph

Fixes #594.

`loadGraphFromJson()` removed all elements and loaded a new graph, but left `graph.pathSource` pointing at a removed node. Path, spiderworm, double star and star path then started from a detached element without any indication why nothing happened.

The path source is now cleared right after removing the old elements.

**generated by OpenCode | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash**

Check the node before logging it in setSource

Fixes #595.

`setSource()` dereferenced the node in its debug log before the null guard, so `setSource(null)` threw a `TypeError` instead of returning `false` as documented. The log line now runs after the guard.

**generated by OpenCode | DeepSeek V4.1 Flash**

fix(pages): keep the spaces around inline links

Closes #323

Same cause as #320. Astro's HTML compression drops the newline before and after an inline link, so the disclaimer read "terms of theGPL-3.0-or-laterlicence" and the licence page "Summary fromTLDRLegal". Explicit `{" "}` keeps the spaces.

The disclaimer also lost the space *after* the link, which the ticket didn't list. Fixed in the same sentence.

Two new e2e tests assert the rendered sentences. Both failed before the fix.

Give class and edge feedback issues useful titles and bodies

Fixes #575.

- Class feedback issues now use `Problem with the class <short name>` as the title instead of the raw URI, consistent with the other generated issues.
- Edge feedback issues keep the readable edge label as title but now list and link source, property, target and (when present) the axiom URI in the body, instead of linking only the source.

Generated by OpenCode

Restore the colored edges option for new views

Fixes #515.

`optionsToJSON()` stores the session option as `coloredEdges`, but `View` read `options.edgesColorized`. The key never exists, so every newly created view applied its style with colored edges disabled, regardless of the checkbox.

The change listener also wrote `config.edgesColorized`, a key nothing reads. That dead assignment is removed; the checkbox state is already available via `Menu.coloredEdges()`.

Generated by OpenCode

Update the layout cache from the toolbar layout buttons

Fixes #518.

The recalculate, tight and compound layout buttons passed `(layoutConfig as any).defaultSubOntologies` to `layout.run()`. `layoutConfig` is the Golden Layout configuration, which has no such property, so `subs` was always `undefined`. `layout.run()` only writes the cache when the subontology list is defined, so manual layouts never refreshed it.

The handlers now pass `config.ontology?.snik?.defaultSubOntologies`, like the equivalent menu entries.

Generated by OpenCode

Handle missing view titles correctly and translate the fallback

Fixes #536.

`View` compared the optional title with the string `"undefined"` instead of the value `undefined`, so the duplicate-title check ran even when no title was given (and a literal title "undefined" was swallowed). The duplicate fallback was also hardcoded German ("Teilmodell") while new views are otherwise titled "Partial Graph". Both the comparison and the title prefixes now use a `partial-graph` language key that exists in English and German.

Generated by OpenCode

Keep all logger arguments

Fixes #580.

The loglevel decorator now forwards every argument to the original method and joins all arguments into a string for the in-memory log and the toast, so exceptions and structured context passed as second arguments are no longer dropped.

Generated by OpenCode

Allow selecting the same file twice in a row

Fixes #570.

`uploadJson()` never cleared the file input value, so after loading a file once the browser did not fire another `change` event when the same file was selected again. Loading a corrected session or layout therefore required choosing a different file first.

Clear the input right after `readAsText()`; the `FileReader` keeps its own reference, so the read is not affected.

Verified with `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx oxlint js/browser/load.ts`.

fix(copy-text): center the icon on the cap height CopyText's copy icon reads low next to its value. The button uses `vertical-align: middle`, which centers it on the x-height of the text. A value like a hostname or port reads as the band from the baseline to the cap line, so the icon sits below it. Lift the button 2px so the icon centers on the cap height instead. The lift uses `top` on the button, which is already relative, so the line box and wrapping stay the same. | Change | Before | After | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | 16px value | | | Red lines mark the cap line and the baseline. Captured from the CopyText e2e fixture in Chromium at 4x. Before sets the button back to `top: 0`, its value on master. ## Terms - Baseline: the line letters sit on. - x-height: the height of lowercase letters with no ascender, like x. - Cap height: the height of capitals. In IBM Plex Sans, digits match. - Cap line: the top of the cap height. CSS defines `middle` as the box's midpoint on the parent's baseline plus half its x-height. That suits lowercase text. Hostnames, IDs and ports are mostly digits and ascenders (d, l, t), so their visual body is the full cap height, and its center is higher. ## Method Measured at 16px IBM Plex Sans on a 24px line, in px from the top of the line. A zero-height inline-block in the value gives the baseline. Canvas `measureText` on "H" and "x" gives the cap height and x-height. `getBBox` on the icon's paths gives its ink. Firefox matches Chromium to 0.01px. | Line | y | | :--- | :--- | | Cap line | 6.8 | | Cap height center | 12.4 | | x-height center | 13.9 | | Baseline | 18.0 | | Icon | Before | After | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Center | 13.9 | 11.9 | | Ink | 6.9 to 20.9 | 4.9 to 18.9 | | Below baseline | 2.9 | 0.9 | The exact lift is half the gap between cap height (0.698em) and x-height (0.516em): 0.091em, or 1.46px at 16px. That is 1.3px at 14px and 1.8px at 20px. The button has `font-size: 0`, so an em offset on it cannot follow the text. A fixed 2px (`$carbon--spacing-01`) stays within 0.75px of exact from 14px to 20px. The extra half pixel also suits the icon. Its front square is the heavier shape and sits low and right, so a geometric center reads low. After the lift, the front square's bottom edge rests on the baseline like a glyph. Lifts of 0, 1.5 and 2px against the cap line and baseline.
